questions.aws: AWS AppConfig feature flags provide managed flags with validation and gradual rollout, and can roll back automatically on CloudWatch alarms.
questions.resume: At Oracle, my Jenkins CLI toolchain added scripted pre-deployment validation so bad releases were caught before rollout. Across the 4 teams that adopted it, failed deploys fell from 11% to 4%.
questions.trap: Treating flags as a substitute for testing. They limit blast radius; they do not prevent the defect.

questions.q: Customers say checkout is slow, and it touches eight microservices. How do you find the cause?
questions.plain: It is like a package that arrives late after passing through eight depots. Instead of interrogating every depot, you read the tracking history, which shows it sat for two days at one depot. Then you go to that depot and ask why.
questions.technical: Start from the symptom metric: confirm which endpoint, which percentile, and since when, and check for a recent deployment or traffic change. Then use distributed tracing. Each request carries a trace ID, and each service records timed spans, so slow traces show which hop dominates, such as a database call or a retry storm against a dependency. Drill into that service's metrics and structured logs filtered by trace ID: query plans, connection pool saturation, throttling, or garbage collection pauses. Fix, then confirm with the same percentile. Common culprits: sequential calls that could run in parallel, missing indexes, N+1 queries, too-short timeouts with retries, and cold caches.

probes.q: What if there is no tracing yet?
probes.a: Correlate request IDs in logs and compare per-service latency metrics. Then add OpenTelemetry instrumentation so next time is faster.

probes.q: How do retries make latency worse?
probes.a: Retries without backoff and jitter multiply load on a struggling dependency. Use timeouts, exponential backoff with jitter, and circuit breakers.

questions.aws: AWS X-Ray traces and service maps, CloudWatch Application Signals, CloudWatch Logs Insights queries filtered by trace ID, and RDS Performance Insights for database waits.
questions.resume: At Oracle, I built real-time API diagnostics across 1M+ endpoints on high-throughput event streams that auto-tagged root causes on 400 and 500 series failures, which cut P1 MTTR from 94 to 26 minutes. Separately, I brought NetSuite search P50 page load down 30%, from 840 to 588 ms, by profiling query plans, restructuring indexes on hot predicates, and rewriting SQL that drove full scans.
questions.trap: Guessing and scaling up everything. Without locating the slow hop, adding capacity often hides the problem or makes a database bottleneck worse.
